transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… the main thing is I’ve just gotten really slow, like noticeably slow. I do hair, and at work it’s like my hands don’t do what they used to do. Even little things that were automatic before—sectioning someone’s hair, getting foils ready, mixing color—feel like I’m moving my hands through glue or something. Like there’s this drag on everything.

And it’s not just me being picky about my work. Other people have started noticing too, which is honestly embarrassing. I used to be pretty quick, or at least normal, and now I’ll realize I’m taking forever on something simple. I’ll be standing there trying to get through a service, and it feels like my body is just… delayed. That’s kind of what made me think I should come in, because it’s affecting my job and people can tell I’m not moving like I used to.
Have you noticed any shaking or tremor in your hands?

I don’t think so… not like a shaking, exactly. I haven’t noticed my hands trembling the way I’d imagine a tremor would look. It’s more that they feel slow or heavy when I’m trying to use them, but I can’t say I’ve seen them visibly shake. If there is any tiny movement, I haven’t really picked up on it.
Have you been feeling depressed lately?

Yeah… I have. Pretty much most days lately, honestly. It’s not even always like crying or some big dramatic thing, it’s more like I wake up and there’s already this heaviness there, like this flat sadness sitting in my chest before anything has even happened. 

And then I start thinking about my life, and it’s like… I had this picture of what I was trying to build, you know? Work, getting better at hair, maybe having my own place feel more settled, just normal things. But lately it feels like there’s no point in trying to build any of it, like I’m already behind or like it’s not going to turn into anything. It’s hard to explain without sounding really negative, but that’s how it feels most mornings.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t seem to?

Um… yeah. Not seeing things, really, I don’t think. But hearing, yes… sometimes. I feel weird saying that out loud because I know how it sounds, but it’s happened enough that I can’t just pretend it’s nothing.

It’s mostly at work, like when I’m doing the boring cleanup stuff after a client—sweeping up hair, rinsing color bowls, wiping things down. I’ll be near the shampoo stations, and I’ll hear this woman’s voice, like she’s close by, saying that I’m ruining everything. It’s not like a thought in my own head exactly… it sounds more like someone nearby said it, so I’ll turn around or look over, but sometimes the salon is empty, or nobody is anywhere near me.

And it’s embarrassing because I’ll kind of freeze for a second and check if someone came in or if one of the other girls said something, but there won’t be anyone there. It makes me feel really unsettled, like I don’t trust the room for a minute. It’s not happening every second or anything, but it’s happened more than once.
Have you ever had a time when you felt unusually high, energized, or wired for days in a row?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve had something like that in the way you mean, like being super energized or wired for days where I’m unstoppable or anything.

I mean, there are times I can’t sleep well or my mind feels kind of busy, but I wouldn’t say I feel “high.” It’s not like I suddenly have tons of energy and feel amazing. If anything, lately I usually feel kind of weighed down. So… no, I don’t think I’ve had days in a row where I felt unusually up or wired.
Have you heard that woman’s voice at times when you were not feeling depressed?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, yes, there was a stretch before the depression got as heavy as it is now where I was still kind of functioning normally. Like I was getting up, going to work, doing clients, keeping up with things more or less. I didn’t feel great, exactly, but it wasn’t that same heavy, hopeless feeling taking over every day yet.

But during that time, I was already hearing her voice sometimes. And it kind of went along with this feeling I had at the salon, like someone there was messing with my schedule or interfering with it somehow. I remember feeling really sure about it, like shifts or appointments were being moved around or handled in a way that was meant to throw me off. And the voice would make it feel even more real, because I’d hear her saying things and then I’d start thinking, “Okay, see, something is happening here.”

So… yeah. It wasn’t only when I was depressed. It started, or at least it was happening, before the depression really took over.
Was there ever a period of at least 2 weeks when you were hearing the woman’s voice even though you were not feeling depressed most of the time?

Yeah… yes, I think it was definitely at least two weeks. It wasn’t just like one weird day or a couple of days. Before the depression really got bad, there was this stretch of several weeks where I was still mostly doing my normal routine—getting up, going into the salon, doing clients, cleaning up, answering people, like… functioning more normally, I guess.

I wasn’t feeling happy, exactly, but I also wasn’t spending most of the time in that really heavy depressed place yet. And during that time, I was already hearing her voice sometimes. It would happen at work, and then I’d start connecting it with things at the salon, like my schedule or appointments feeling like they were being messed with. I remember feeling pretty sure someone there was interfering with it, like not just a mistake, but on purpose.

So, yeah… if you mean hearing the voice while I wasn’t depressed most of the time, then yes. There was a period like that, and it lasted several weeks.
Have the voice and the feeling that people at the salon were interfering with your schedule been going on for at least 6 months?

Yes… it’s definitely been more than six months. It’s been, I think, about a year and four months now since the voice started happening and since I started feeling like someone was targeting my bookings or messing with my schedule at the salon.

It’s hard to say the exact date because it didn’t feel like one clear moment where everything suddenly started. It was more like little things at first, like I’d notice something off with the appointments or I’d hear her voice and then I’d start putting it together. But if I’m being honest, this has been going on for around a year and four months, not just a few months.
Since this started, have you been doing noticeably worse overall at work or in taking care of yourself than you used to?

Yeah… yes. I mean, I don’t like admitting that, because I used to be really reliable at work. Like, I was the person who remembered little things for clients, kept my station clean, stayed on top of timing, all of that. But since this started, I’ve definitely been doing worse.

At the salon, I make mistakes with really basic routines now, things I shouldn’t mess up—like mixing up small steps, forgetting what I already set out, taking too long to finish things that used to feel automatic. I’m slower with clients, and then I get nervous because I can tell they notice. My manager has lost trust in me, I think. She doesn’t say it in a cruel way, but she checks on me more, or hesitates before giving me certain appointments, and that feels awful because I know I wasn’t like that before.

And with clients too… some of them don’t book with me as much, or they seem less comfortable. I’ve canceled things I used to always handle, even simple appointments or helping with cleanup or extra tasks. I used to be dependable, and now I feel like people don’t really count on me the same way.

Outside of work, I’ve pulled away from friends a lot. I don’t answer messages like I used to, and I don’t really go out. I also stopped showing up for the volunteer haircuts I used to do at the senior center, which I feel guilty about, because I actually cared about that. It’s just like… overall I’m not functioning the way I used to.
Have you noticed yourself talking much less than you used to?

Yeah… I have. I don’t know if I noticed it at first, because I’m still technically talking at work when I have to, like asking what someone wants done with their hair or answering a basic question. But compared to how I used to be, it’s really different.

I used to chat with clients the whole appointment sometimes—about their kids, vacations, shows, just little normal salon stuff. I’d remember details and ask follow-up questions, and it came naturally. I also used to help the newer stylists, like if they were nervous or unsure about something, I’d step in and talk them through it. I liked being that person.

Now I mostly keep my head down. I say what I need to say, but I don’t really start conversations. If a client is quiet, I’m almost relieved because then I don’t have to pretend I have that energy. And even with friends, I used to go hiking and talk for hours, or make plans, or just send dumb messages during the day. Now I avoid people more. It’s not that I hate them or anything, I just… I don’t have that spark in me. Talking feels like it takes effort I don’t really have.
Have other people commented that your face looks less expressive or that your voice sounds flatter than it used to?

I don’t know if anyone has said it exactly like that, like “your face looks flat” or “your voice is monotone.” Not in those words, at least. But people have definitely noticed that I’m not as… animated, I guess.

At work, I used to be really chatty with clients. Like I’d smile more, ask them about their lives, remember little things, joke around a bit, and it felt natural. I’d also help the newer stylists and kind of talk them through things if they were nervous. Now I mostly keep my head down and just say what I have to say to get through the appointment. So even if nobody says, “your face looks less expressive,” I can tell they feel the difference.

Friends have noticed too. I used to go hiking with them and talk a lot, or make plans and actually sound excited. Now I avoid people more, and I think I probably do sound flatter because I just don’t have that spark in me like I used to. It’s not like I’m trying to be cold or rude. It just takes so much effort to seem normal.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah… I have. It’s kind of embarrassing to say because some of the things I used to enjoy were such normal parts of who I was, and now they feel like chores or like I’m watching somebody else do them from far away.

At work, I used to actually enjoy talking with clients. Not just the haircut part, but the whole back-and-forth—asking about their family, remembering some little thing they told me last time, joking around, making them feel comfortable. I liked helping the newer stylists too, like if someone was nervous or unsure, I’d step in and talk them through it. That used to make me feel useful, like I had a place there.

Now I mostly just keep my head down and try to get through the appointment. I don’t really start conversations unless I have to. If someone wants to chat, I feel this pressure to respond the right way, and I just don’t have that same spark in me. It’s not that I suddenly dislike them, it’s more like the interest or energy that used to come naturally just isn’t there.

And with friends, yeah… I used to go hiking and actually look forward to it. I’d talk the whole time, make plans, take pictures, send messages afterward. Now I avoid people a lot more. Even if someone invites me, I’ll put off answering because the idea of going and acting like myself feels exhausting. So yes, I’ve lost interest, or maybe lost the ability to feel interested the way I used to.
Have you ever had a period when you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy?

I’m not really sure. I mean… I’ve had plenty of nights where I didn’t sleep well, or I stayed up too late and then had to drag myself through the next day, but that’s different from feeling full of energy.

If you mean like sleeping only a few hours and then waking up feeling amazing or unstoppable or like I didn’t need sleep at all… I don’t think so. At least nothing that stands out to me that way. Usually if I get less sleep, I feel it. I get tired, slower, more worn down. It’s not like I suddenly have all this extra energy.
Have you ever had a head injury, seizure, or another neurological illness?

I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve bumped my head like anyone has, probably, but not anything I’d call a real head injury or anything where I had to be treated for it.

No seizures that I know of. And I haven’t been told I have some neurological illness or anything like that. I guess I’m not totally sure what all counts as neurological, but nothing comes to mind—no diagnosis or major event like that.
Have you been using methamphetamine, cocaine, or any other drugs around the times when you hear the woman’s voice?

I don’t think so… I mean, no, not that I can connect to it. I haven’t noticed it being tied to anything like that.

When it happens, I don’t sit there thinking, “Oh, this is because I took something,” or anything like that. I guess I’d say I’m not aware of using meth or cocaine around those times. I’m trying to think carefully because I don’t want to answer wrong, but there isn’t some pattern I can point to where I hear her voice after using drugs.

I’m sorry if that’s not a very clear answer. It’s just… from what I can tell, no, I haven’t noticed drug use being part of when it happens.
Have you ever had a period lasting several days when you felt unusually euphoric or irritable?

I’m not sure… I mean, I’ve definitely been irritable for several days before, but I don’t know if I’d call it unusual in the way you mean. Like, if I’m stressed or overwhelmed, I can get snappy or kind of on edge for a while, but it doesn’t feel like some totally different version of me, if that makes sense.

As far as euphoric… I don’t really think so. I don’t remember a stretch of several days where I was just unusually happy or high or anything like that. I’ve had good moods, obviously, and times where I felt better than usual, but not in a way that seemed extreme or like other people were concerned.

I guess I’m trying to separate normal mood stuff from what you’re asking. If you mean several days where I was so happy or so irritable that it really stood out as abnormal, I can’t think of a clear time like that.
Does the woman’s voice ever say things that are not about you ruining things or being worthless?

Mostly it’s about that… about me ruining things, or being worthless, or like I’m messing everything up. That’s the main thing I hear.

It’ll happen at work sometimes when I’m doing really normal stuff, like sweeping up hair or rinsing out color bowls, and I’ll hear this woman’s voice kind of near the shampoo stations. And it feels like it’s nearby, not like I’m just thinking it. She’ll say I’m ruining everything, or that I can’t do anything right. Sometimes the salon is empty, or there’s nobody close enough to be saying it, which is what makes it so upsetting.

I’m trying to think if she says other things… but honestly, I don’t think there’s a lot outside of that theme. It’s usually critical, like about me being worthless or messing everything up.
Have you ever had a belief that people were trying to harm you or interfere with you in a way that was not about you being worthless or ruining things?

I mean… yes, kind of. I know this is going to sound strange, and I don’t really like saying it out loud because it makes me feel like I’m being dramatic, but I’ve had this feeling that someone at the salon is watching my bookings and messing with my hours on purpose.

Like, I’ll talk about needing to save money, or how I’m trying to get ahead on bills, and then right after that it feels like my schedule suddenly gets weirdly slow. Not just normal slow, but like the days I need clients the most, those are the days where my bookings disappear or I don’t get put on the right hours. And I start thinking, how would that happen unless someone was interfering?

It doesn’t feel exactly like people are trying to physically hurt me or anything, but it does feel like someone is trying to block me or mess with me, like they don’t want me to do well. I know it may not make sense from the outside, but when it keeps lining up that way, it’s hard for me not to think it’s on purpose.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being controlled by someone else?

I don’t know if I’d say controlled exactly, like someone putting thoughts into my head or moving them around like a remote control… that doesn’t feel like the right way to describe it.

It’s more that I get really convinced someone at the salon is interfering with things around me. Like my bookings and my hours. I know that’s not exactly what you asked, but that’s the closest thing I can think of. I’ll mention needing to save money or trying to catch up on bills, and then suddenly my schedule gets slow in this way that feels too specific. Like the slow days happen right after I talk about it, and it makes me feel like someone has been watching my bookings and messing with my hours on purpose.

So not my thoughts being controlled, no… but I do feel like someone is kind of messing with my life or trying to block me, if that makes sense.
When you were in that heavy depressed state, were you still hearing the woman’s voice?

Yes… when the sadness got really heavy, I was still hearing it. It wasn’t like the voice was only happening when I was feeling okay and then the depression came later, or the other way around. They were sort of happening at the same time.

Like, when I was in that really low place where everything felt heavy and stuck, I would still hear the woman’s voice around the shampoo stations, saying those things about me ruining everything or being worthless. And at the same time, I was also getting really caught up in the idea that someone was messing with my bookings or my hours on purpose. So it all kind of blended together — the depression, the voice, and feeling like someone was trying to sabotage me at work.

It didn’t feel separate in my head. It felt like while I was already really down, those things were also going on, which made it feel even harder to get out of.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking how long the hallucinations and delusional belief about salon schedule interference have been going on, which matches the psychotic symptoms duration.

patient.answer:
Yes… it’s definitely been more than six months. It’s been, I think, about a year and four months now since the voice started happening and since I started feeling like someone was targeting my bookings or messing with my schedule at the salon.

It’s hard to say the exact date because it didn’t feel like one clear moment where everything suddenly started. It was more like little things at first, like I’d notice something off with the appointments or I’d hear her voice and then I’d start putting it together. But if I’m being honest, this has been going on for around a year and four months, not just a few months.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been a sustained decline in overall functioning, which best distinguishes schizophrenia from schizoaffective disorder or psychotic depression at this point.
doctor.question: Since this started, have you been doing noticeably worse overall at work or in taking care of yourself than you used to?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I have lost trust from my manager and clients because I make mistakes with basic salon routines, work too slowly, and cancel things I used to reliably handle. I have also pulled away from friends and stopped showing up for volunteer haircuts at the senior center.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about decline in overall functioning at work and self-care since symptoms started, which directly matches functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Yeah… yes. I mean, I don’t like admitting that, because I used to be really reliable at work. Like, I was the person who remembered little things for clients, kept my station clean, stayed on top of timing, all of that. But since this started, I’ve definitely been doing worse.

At the salon, I make mistakes with really basic routines now, things I shouldn’t mess up—like mixing up small steps, forgetting what I already set out, taking too long to finish things that used to feel automatic. I’m slower with clients, and then I get nervous because I can tell they notice. My manager has lost trust in me, I think. She doesn’t say it in a cruel way, but she checks on me more, or hesitates before giving me certain appointments, and that feels awful because I know I wasn’t like that before.

And with clients too… some of them don’t book with me as much, or they seem less comfortable. I’ve canceled things I used to always handle, even simple appointments or helping with cleanup or extra tasks. I used to be dependable, and now I feel like people don’t really count on me the same way.

Outside of work, I’ve pulled away from friends a lot. I don’t answer messages like I used to, and I don’t really go out. I also stopped showing up for the volunteer haircuts I used to do at the senior center, which I feel guilty about, because I actually cared about that. It’s just like… overall I’m not functioning the way I used to.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there have been prominent negative symptoms, which helps distinguish schizophrenia from schizoaffective disorder or psychotic depression.
doctor.question: Have you noticed yourself talking much less than you used to?

target_item.name: Negative_Symptoms
target_item.manifestation: I used to chat with clients, help the newer stylists, and go hiking with friends, but now I mostly keep my head down and avoid people because I just don’t have that spark in me.
target_item.reason: The question asks about talking much less than before, which directly relates to diminished speech/social engagement under negative symptoms.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I have. I don’t know if I noticed it at first, because I’m still technically talking at work when I have to, like asking what someone wants done with their hair or answering a basic question. But compared to how I used to be, it’s really different.

I used to chat with clients the whole appointment sometimes—about their kids, vacations, shows, just little normal salon stuff. I’d remember details and ask follow-up questions, and it came naturally. I also used to help the newer stylists, like if they were nervous or unsure about something, I’d step in and talk them through it. I liked being that person.

Now I mostly keep my head down. I say what I need to say, but I don’t really start conversations. If a client is quiet, I’m almost relieved because then I don’t have to pretend I have that energy. And even with friends, I used to go hiking and talk for hours, or make plans, or just send dumb messages during the day. Now I avoid people more. It’s not that I hate them or anything, I just… I don’t have that spark in me. Talking feels like it takes effort I don’t really have.

doctor.intent: Assess for flat or blunted affect to help distinguish schizophrenia from schizoaffective disorder with depression or psychotic depression.
doctor.question: Have other people commented that your face looks less expressive or that your voice sounds flatter than it used to?

target_item.name: Negative_Symptoms
target_item.manifestation: I used to chat with clients, help the newer stylists, and go hiking with friends, but now I mostly keep my head down and avoid people because I just don’t have that spark in me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about reduced facial expressiveness and flatter voice, which are diminished emotional expression and fit negative symptoms.

patient.answer:
I don’t know if anyone has said it exactly like that, like “your face looks flat” or “your voice is monotone.” Not in those words, at least. But people have definitely noticed that I’m not as… animated, I guess.

At work, I used to be really chatty with clients. Like I’d smile more, ask them about their lives, remember little things, joke around a bit, and it felt natural. I’d also help the newer stylists and kind of talk them through things if they were nervous. Now I mostly keep my head down and just say what I have to say to get through the appointment. So even if nobody says, “your face looks less expressive,” I can tell they feel the difference.

Friends have noticed too. I used to go hiking with them and talk a lot, or make plans and actually sound excited. Now I avoid people more, and I think I probably do sound flatter because I just don’t have that spark in me like I used to. It’s not like I’m trying to be cold or rude. It just takes so much effort to seem normal.

inference.note: This turn adds prominent negative symptoms/affective flattening (reduced speech, less animation) alongside >6 months of psychosis and functional decline, increasing likelihood of F20.9; however it does not fully exclude schizoaffective, mood disorder with psychotic features, bipolar disorder, or organic psychosis yet.

doctor.intent: Assess for prominent negative symptoms to help distinguish schizophrenia from schizoaffective disorder or mood disorder with psychotic features.
doctor.question: Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

target_item.name: Negative_Symptoms
target_item.manifestation: I used to chat with clients, help the newer stylists, and go hiking with friends, but now I mostly keep my head down and avoid people because I just don’t have that spark in me.
target_item.reason: The question asks about loss of interest in previously enjoyable activities, which is most directly covered by diminished motivation and social interest in this profile.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I have. It’s kind of embarrassing to say because some of the things I used to enjoy were such normal parts of who I was, and now they feel like chores or like I’m watching somebody else do them from far away.

At work, I used to actually enjoy talking with clients. Not just the haircut part, but the whole back-and-forth—asking about their family, remembering some little thing they told me last time, joking around, making them feel comfortable. I liked helping the newer stylists too, like if someone was nervous or unsure, I’d step in and talk them through it. That used to make me feel useful, like I had a place there.

Now I mostly just keep my head down and try to get through the appointment. I don’t really start conversations unless I have to. If someone wants to chat, I feel this pressure to respond the right way, and I just don’t have that same spark in me. It’s not that I suddenly dislike them, it’s more like the interest or energy that used to come naturally just isn’t there.

And with friends, yeah… I used to go hiking and actually look forward to it. I’d talk the whole time, make plans, take pictures, send messages afterward. Now I avoid people a lot more. Even if someone invites me, I’ll put off answering because the idea of going and acting like myself feels exhausting. So yes, I’ve lost interest, or maybe lost the ability to feel interested the way I used to.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are prominent manic symptoms to rule in schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type or bipolar disorder with psychotic features versus schizophrenia.
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period when you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy?

target_item.reason: The question asks about a possible manic or hypomanic symptom—decreased need for sleep with increased energy—which is not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I’m not really sure. I mean… I’ve had plenty of nights where I didn’t sleep well, or I stayed up too late and then had to drag myself through the next day, but that’s different from feeling full of energy.

If you mean like sleeping only a few hours and then waking up feeling amazing or unstoppable or like I didn’t need sleep at all… I don’t think so. At least nothing that stands out to me that way. Usually if I get less sleep, I feel it. I get tired, slower, more worn down. It’s not like I suddenly have all this extra energy.

doctor.intent: Determine whether psychotic symptoms are due to a medical/neurological condition rather than a primary psychotic or mood disorder.
doctor.question: Have you ever had a head injury, seizure, or another neurological illness?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about history of head injury, seizures, or neurological illness, which is not covered by any symptom profile item provided.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve bumped my head like anyone has, probably, but not anything I’d call a real head injury or anything where I had to be treated for it.

No seizures that I know of. And I haven’t been told I have some neurological illness or anything like that. I guess I’m not totally sure what all counts as neurological, but nothing comes to mind—no diagnosis or major event like that.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the psychosis could be substance/medication-induced rather than schizophrenia/schizoaffective disorder.
doctor.question: Have you been using methamphetamine, cocaine, or any other drugs around the times when you hear the woman’s voice?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about substance or drug use around the time of hearing the voice, and the symptom profile does not include substance use or intoxication-related information.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so… I mean, no, not that I can connect to it. I haven’t noticed it being tied to anything like that.

When it happens, I don’t sit there thinking, “Oh, this is because I took something,” or anything like that. I guess I’d say I’m not aware of using meth or cocaine around those times. I’m trying to think carefully because I don’t want to answer wrong, but there isn’t some pattern I can point to where I hear her voice after using drugs.

I’m sorry if that’s not a very clear answer. It’s just… from what I can tell, no, I haven’t noticed drug use being part of when it happens.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether there have been any mood episodes meeting criteria for mania, to distinguish schizophrenia/schizoaffective disorder from bipolar disorder with psychotic features.
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period lasting several days when you felt unusually euphoric or irritable?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about possible manic or hypomanic mood elevation/irritability lasting several days, but the provided symptom profile does not include a mania or hypomania item.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure… I mean, I’ve definitely been irritable for several days before, but I don’t know if I’d call it unusual in the way you mean. Like, if I’m stressed or overwhelmed, I can get snappy or kind of on edge for a while, but it doesn’t feel like some totally different version of me, if that makes sense.

As far as euphoric… I don’t really think so. I don’t remember a stretch of several days where I was just unusually happy or high or anything like that. I’ve had good moods, obviously, and times where I felt better than usual, but not in a way that seemed extreme or like other people were concerned.

I guess I’m trying to separate normal mood stuff from what you’re asking. If you mean several days where I was so happy or so irritable that it really stood out as abnormal, I can’t think of a clear time like that.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether the psychotic symptoms are mood-incongruent and not limited to depressive themes, to better distinguish schizophrenia from schizoaffective disorder with depressive episodes.
doctor.question: Does the woman’s voice ever say things that are not about you ruining things or being worthless?

target_item.name: Hallucinations
target_item.manifestation: Sometimes when I’m sweeping up or rinsing bowls, I hear a woman’s voice near the shampoo stations saying I’m ruining everything, even when the salon is empty or nobody is close by.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the content and nature of the woman’s voice, which is an auditory hallucination.

patient.answer:
Mostly it’s about that… about me ruining things, or being worthless, or like I’m messing everything up. That’s the main thing I hear.

It’ll happen at work sometimes when I’m doing really normal stuff, like sweeping up hair or rinsing out color bowls, and I’ll hear this woman’s voice kind of near the shampoo stations. And it feels like it’s nearby, not like I’m just thinking it. She’ll say I’m ruining everything, or that I can’t do anything right. Sometimes the salon is empty, or there’s nobody close enough to be saying it, which is what makes it so upsetting.

I’m trying to think if she says other things… but honestly, I don’t think there’s a lot outside of that theme. It’s usually critical, like about me being worthless or messing everything up.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms are exclusively mood-congruent, which helps distinguish schizoaffective/schizophrenia from major depressive disorder with psychotic features.
doctor.question: Have you ever had a belief that people were trying to harm you or interfere with you in a way that was not about you being worthless or ruining things?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I know it sounds strange, but I’m pretty sure someone at the salon has been watching my bookings and messing with my hours on purpose, because the slow days seem to happen right after I talk about saving money.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about fixed beliefs that others are trying to harm or interfere with the patient, which directly matches delusions.

patient.answer:
I mean… yes, kind of. I know this is going to sound strange, and I don’t really like saying it out loud because it makes me feel like I’m being dramatic, but I’ve had this feeling that someone at the salon is watching my bookings and messing with my hours on purpose.

Like, I’ll talk about needing to save money, or how I’m trying to get ahead on bills, and then right after that it feels like my schedule suddenly gets weirdly slow. Not just normal slow, but like the days I need clients the most, those are the days where my bookings disappear or I don’t get put on the right hours. And I start thinking, how would that happen unless someone was interfering?

It doesn’t feel exactly like people are trying to physically hurt me or anything, but it does feel like someone is trying to block me or mess with me, like they don’t want me to do well. I know it may not make sense from the outside, but when it keeps lining up that way, it’s hard for me not to think it’s on purpose.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms are limited to mood-congruent content or include bizarre/disorganized features more suggestive of schizophrenia.
doctor.question: Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being controlled by someone else?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I know it sounds strange, but I’m pretty sure someone at the salon has been watching my bookings and messing with my hours on purpose, because the slow days seem to happen right after I talk about saving money.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about a possible delusional belief involving external control of thoughts, which falls under delusions.

patient.answer:
I don’t know if I’d say controlled exactly, like someone putting thoughts into my head or moving them around like a remote control… that doesn’t feel like the right way to describe it.

It’s more that I get really convinced someone at the salon is interfering with things around me. Like my bookings and my hours. I know that’s not exactly what you asked, but that’s the closest thing I can think of. I’ll mention needing to save money or trying to catch up on bills, and then suddenly my schedule gets slow in this way that feels too specific. Like the slow days happen right after I talk about it, and it makes me feel like someone has been watching my bookings and messing with my hours on purpose.

So not my thoughts being controlled, no… but I do feel like someone is kind of messing with my life or trying to block me, if that makes sense.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether psychotic symptoms have ever occurred during a major depressive episode, which helps distinguish schizophrenia from schizoaffective disorder and psychotic depression.
doctor.question: When you were in that heavy depressed state, were you still hearing the woman’s voice?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: When the sadness got heavy and stayed, the voice at the shampoo stations and the belief that someone was sabotaging my bookings were happening at the same time, not separately.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the hallucination occurred during the heavy depressed state, which directly addresses whether psychotic symptoms and the depressive episode happened at the same time.

patient.answer:
Yes… when the sadness got really heavy, I was still hearing it. It wasn’t like the voice was only happening when I was feeling okay and then the depression came later, or the other way around. They were sort of happening at the same time.

Like, when I was in that really low place where everything felt heavy and stuck, I would still hear the woman’s voice around the shampoo stations, saying those things about me ruining everything or being worthless. And at the same time, I was also getting really caught up in the idea that someone was messing with my bookings or my hours on purpose. So it all kind of blended together — the depression, the voice, and feeling like someone was trying to sabotage me at work.

It didn’t feel separate in my head. It felt like while I was already really down, those things were also going on, which made it feel even harder to get out of.

opening_question.intent: Open the interview by learning the patient's main reason for seeking care today
opening_question.question: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: Psychotic symptoms (recurrent auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusional beliefs) have been present for over 6 months with functional decline, and there was a period of several weeks with hallucinations/delusions occurring in the absence of a major depressive episode. A depressive syndrome is also present for much of the illness, making schizoaffective disorder more likely than schizophrenia or major depressive disorder with psychotic features. No clear history of manic/hypomanic episodes, substance cause, or neurological cause was established.
